In summary, our research is concerned with
development of a new strategy to produce in yeast functionally active recombinant antibody fragments with improved stability and avidity.
development of new recombinant vaccine against VLY-mediated bacterial vaginosis.
the development of new recombinant vaccine candidates and diagnostic reagents against vaginosis-causing pathogen Gardnerella vaginalis and other bacterial pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of recombinant scFvs in yeast is a very challenging and difficult task.
the yeast expression system can be used to produce pseudotype virus-like particle harboring functionally-active scFv-Fcs.
the scFv protein fused with human IgGFc and produced in yeast was not soluble and therefore was not suitable for purification and activity testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the yeast system can be used to produce pseudotype VLP harboring functionally intact antibody fragment.
we developed a novel approach to produce high-affinity sc-Fv-Fc protein neutralizing VLY cytolytic activity in the form of VLPs.
we have demonstrated for the first and the only time in the world that pseudotype VLP can serve as an effective platform for production of recombinant antibodies with high antigen-binding potency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production and purification of high-affinity scfv-Fc proteins can be significantly facilitated by their multimeric display on the surface of the recombinant virus-like particles.
the yeast expression system can be used for production of pseudotype VLY-neutralizing VLPs.
pseudotype virus-like particle technology can be used for the production and delivery of high-potency neutralizing antibody fragments.
